correctness.rationale: Averaging over simultaneous index permutations and side interchange is permitted because the SLEM is the operator norm of \(P-J\), hence convex. The full invariant spectrum consists of 1, 1-(2m+1)a, 1-a-2(m-1)b, 1-a-(m-2)b with multiplicity m-1, and 1-a-mb with multiplicity m-1. The exact positive combination \(2(m-1)[1-a-(m-2)b]-(m-2)[1-a-2(m-1)b]=m(1-a)\) gives \(\mu\ge(2m-1)/(2(3m-4))\). Proposed positive weights saturate and their remaining modes are bounded. Uniqueness without symmetry follows by equality in the PSD spectral-norm bound on the active positive (m-1)-dimensional eigenspace and active negative vector; row/column restrictions force all cross-edge weights equal for \(m\ge4\) and then all hub weights. Standalone tests: 324 exact rational identities, 72 direct spectra, five exact characteristic polynomials, 840 random feasible comparisons; the proof is not inferred from finite computations.

originality.rationale: The wheel result of Boyd et al. 2009 covers the \(m=3\) cone over the six-cycle, so it is excluded. For \(m\ge4\) the graph is \(K_1\) joined to a non-cycle crown, not a complete multipartite graph or a pair of cliques connected by a bridge. The source paper gives general symmetry and spectrum methods but neither these exact optimal probabilities nor uniqueness against all nonsymmetric kernels. Mathematical-record and external literature searches found no direct coverage, and accessible prior local claims concern distinct graph families. This is evidence-based best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness guarantee.
residual_risks: An unindexed manuscript, stronger general cone theorem, or an uninspected appendix elsewhere could imply the exact result.
The primary-paper comparison is focused on the directly relevant sections and examples, not a claim that all mathematical papers have been exhaustively read.

value.rationale: The cone over a crown is a natural network with one universal hub and a systematically removed cross-part matching, including the cone over the three-dimensional cube as its smallest new case. The theorem specifies every edge probability and all loop weights on the entire unbounded family, proves every available communication edge receives positive mass, and establishes global uniqueness among arbitrary asymmetric placements of edge probabilities (while matrices remain symmetric). This distinction is not obtained from automorphism averaging alone: invariant optimality does not rule out nonsymmetric optimal kernels. The exact asymptotic SLEM 1/3 and hub saturation quantify the role of the apex.
